Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 
April, 2024 
Author: Rahul Bharti
Bench: Rahul Bharti
 High Court Of Jammu &Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Srinagar
 Reserved on: 09.11.2023
 Pronounced on: 03.04.2024
 Owp No. 19/2018
Shahbaz Sultan and others
 ... Petitioner/Appellant(s)
Through: Mr. Kaiser Ali, Advocate
 V/s
Union of India and others
 ... Respondent(s)
Through: Mr. T. M. Shamsi, Dsgi with Ms. Yaseema Jan, Advocate
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge
 Order
03-04-2024 1. A misplaced and/or undeserving equity extended at some point of time in the past, be it by default or design, in favour of a person with respect to use of State's property/asset cannot be taken to be a matter of use for all time to come in the field of public administration concerning the administration and allotment of state property/assets. 
2. The petitioners, through the medium of this writ petition, are literally seeking a perpetual extension of a misplaced equity which was once shown individually in their favour at some point of time in past with respect to the use and occupation of the shop-spaces in STC BSF Campus Humhama, Srinagar, and for that are seeking this court, under article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue writ of certiorari, mandamus and prohibition so as to checkmate the respondents from going ahead with intended public auction exercise for the shops housed in the STC BSF Complex Humhama Srinagar.
3. Border Security Force, BSF, has a campus at Humhama, Srinagar which is a Subsidiary Training Centre (STC) housing BSF trainees/personnel and officers on regular basis. In routine reference it is Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
1 known as STC BSF Campus Humhama, Srinagar. 
4. In order to cater to needs/requirements of the BSF trainees/personnels/officers in terms daily use amenities/ items/eatables/household articles/wares so as to be available within the STC BSF Campus, some shops, with permanent structure and some makeshift ones, are provided at the said campus. At present, there are said to be 17 odd number of shops at the STC BSF Campus to become a sort of a shopping complex meant for shopping only by BSF personnels. However, the spaces of these shops are let out to the civilian vendors/shopkeepers for retail business of identified commodities/services so as to provide in- house shopping facility to the campus inmates for the sake of safety and security of the STC BSF Campus and the personnels stationed inside. 
5. The petitioners, who are 14 in numbers, joined together to institute the present writ petition filed on 09/01/2018 bearing the status and claim of being in use and occupation of the shops in the said BSF STC Campus, Humhama, and with a purported common cause of action emanating from an issuance of a tender notice No. Prov/Tender-Shop/STC-KMR/2017/19226-35 dated 30/12/2017 by the office of the IG, STC, BSF Kashmir, Srinagar, for the purpose of public auction for renting out the civil shops in the said shopping complex of STC BSF Campus, Humhama for a period of 11 months from the date of issue of allotment order or signing the agreement which everbeing earlier. 
In terms of the said tender notice, all the shops available in the shopping complex of STC BSF Campus Humhama were meant to be put to public auction in order to fetch highest rent bidders. 
6. The petitioners, being in purported use and occupation of some of the shops in the said STC BSF Campus Humhama, reckoned said tender notice to be prejudicial to their purported entitlement to stay in use and occupation of the respective shops held by them and therefore came forward to lay the present petition asking therein in the following reliefs:
"(i) Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Certiorari in favour of petitioners and against the respondents by quashing the impugned tender notice dated 30.12.2017 forming Annexure G to the writ petition.
(ii) Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Prohibition Prohibiting the respondents from giving any effect to the impugned tender notice dated 30.12.2017 unless and until decision is not taken upon the representation submitted by them forming part of this writ petition and also unless and until proper procedure and law is not followed by them.
(iii) Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Mandamus, commanding the respondent to allow the petitioners to run their shops allotted to them for conducting their respective businesses without taking recourse of impugned tender notice and also accept the future rentals from the petitioners as have been accepted by the respondents as on today as reflected in the annexure annexed with the writ petition.
(iv) Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Mandamus, commanding the respondents to adhere to the promise extended to the petitioners by them while Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
2 issuing the allotment orders and also while accepting the one-time rental dues from the petitioners for the period for which no rentals were fixed as reflected in Annexure B and also produce whole record pertaining to the process initiated by them while issuing the impugned tender notice whether the law governing the field and also whether the already promise extended to the petitioners has been strictly followed or not before this Hon'ble court for its onwards consideration and appropriate orders.
(v) The Hon'ble Court may pass any other order or direction, which it deems just and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case."
7. In order to claim grant of said reliefs in their favour, the petitioners have come forward setting up a narrative that the petitioners, being unemployed, started their business in the shops temporarily constructed by the respondents way back in the year 1990 and thereafter allotted the same to the petitioners with an understanding that the petitioners would be providing various items to the families of the respondents' employees posted at Srinagar. 
8. It is meant to be pleaded and suggested in the writ petition by the petitioners that it is they who had volunteered to run the shops for the purpose of serving the families of the BSF personnel housed in the STC BSF Campus, Humhama as there were no takers for the said shops to do business and that is how the shops were made available to the petitioners without any rentals. 
9. It is pleaded that up to year 2013 the petitioners were running the shops without any rental payment but then from nowhere the respondents issued notices for recovery of old dues of rent and electricity charges against the petitioners directing them to pay the rentals as well as electricity charges right from the year 2010 up to October 2013 and seeking the deposit in one go along with future rental and electricity charges for the next three months starting from October 2013 onwards. 
10. By reference to the notices so issued to them, the petitioners came to plead that they were authorized to hold the shops for 11 months with an attending assurance that they would be charged 10% hike of the rental after every 11 months. The petitioners claim that they made the deposits of the earlier rent dues as per the respective notices issued and also making periodic rental payments so as to carry on their business at the shops allotted to them. 
11. For the purpose of showing their respective allotment of the shops, the petitioners have annexed along with the writ petition in the form of annexure-A the allotment orders but without pleading in the writ petition as to which allotment order so annexed pertains to which particular petitioner.
Following are the allotment orders so annexed:
a) Order No. 1005/Adm/BWWA/MN/2013 dated 10/10/2013 of the IG BSF FTR. HQ KMR in favour of firm M/s Kingfisher Tour and Travels, Airport Humhama authorizing supply/providing SIM card, E-Ticketing & Photocopier facilities. 
b) Order No. 1005/Adm/selling/Ftr KMR/15/4881-82 dated 30/01/2015 of the IG BSF FTR. HQ KMR in favour of M/s Angel Nidouz Food Court.

3 c) Order No. Prov/shop rent/STC-SGR/2016/3263-64 dated 24/02/2016 of the office of DIG STC. BSF SGR in favour of M/s Basharat Cloth Shop;
d) Order No. Prov/shop rent/STC-SGR/2016/3261-62 dated 24/02/2016 of the office of DIG STC. BSF SGR in favour of M/s Adil Gift & Stationary Shop;
e) Letter No. Prov/STC-SGR/Auction/2017/4429-30 dated 30/03/2017 of the Office of IG STC BSF Srinagar Kashmir in favour of M/s Md.
Ashraf Lone (Irfan) Stationary & Gift Shop-II [ Md. Ashraf Lone];
f) Letter No. Prov/Civil Shop/STC-SGR/2015/6675 of the Office of DIG STC BSF Srinagar in favour of M/s Govind Tailor Shop;
g) Letter No. Prov/shop rent/STC-SGR/2016/3253-54 dated24/02/2016 of the office of DIG STC BSF Srinagar in favour of M/s Govind Tailor Shop;
h) Letter No. Prov/shop rent/STC-SGR/2016/3235-36 dated 24/02/2016 of the office of DIG STC BSF Srinagar in favour of M/s Govind Tailor Shop;
i) Undated and un-numbered Permission Identity Card stamped by Quarter Master STC BSF KMR in favour of M/s Irfan Studio Prop. Mohammad Ashraf Lone. 
12. By reference to these seven documents, all fourteen (14) writ petitioners are expecting this court to read their respective allotment of shops in the STC BSF Shopping complex without further pleading as to how each and every petitioner first came to be in use and occupation of respective shop for business purpose and on the allotment order/approval of which BSF official/authority. 
Except a bald averment in the writ petition that from year 1990s onwards the petitioners have been running shops in the STC BSF Campus, Humhama, the writ petitioners have taken least, rather, no trouble to plead that for how long their respective use and occupation qua respective shop has been in currency for enabling them to claim a long-term future use and occupation of the shops in the said STC BSF Campus literally amounting to self- given perpetual lease/allotment in their favour. In fact, this is the tone and tenor of the writ petition if read between the lines, and that gets exhibited and exposed from the nature of the reliefs claimed in the writ petition and as reproduced here in before. 
13. The petitioners have pleaded that while they had all cleared their rent arrears demanded in terms of the notices served to them but again in the year 2016 they came to be informed by the respondents that there is going to take place at a onetime auction with respect to the shops allotted to the petitioners for the sake of maintenance of record as was being done in other States and said procedure was being adopted, so the petitioners, having invested money and loan investment in the business being conducted at the said shops, accepted the said proposition of the respondents which was purportedly with an assurance that the petitioners upon getting the shops in auction will be charged rentals to be determined by CPWD every year with 10% hike and would stay in use and Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
4 occupation for all time to come.
14. In this regard, the petitioners have referred to a communication No. Prov/STC-SGR/Notice/Civil Shops/2016/21739-55 dated 28/12/2016 of the office of DIG STC BSF Srinagar Kashmir addressed to 17 concerns named therein which are as under:
1. M/s Kingfisher Tours and Travels 2. M / s Angle Nidouz Food Court. 
3. M/s Govind Tailor Shop,
4. M/s Deshraj Sharma (Meat Shop)
5. M/s Deshraj Sharma (Veg. Shop)
6. M / s Basharat Cloth House 7. M/s Farooq Dry Fruit Shop 8. M/s Adil Stat & Gift Shop 9. M/s Govind Tailor 10. M/s Javed Akhtar Tailor Shop 11. M/s Krishan Lal Cobbler Shop 12. M/s Shyam Lal Cobbler Shop 13. M/s Md Ashraf Lone (Irfan), Stat & Gen Store 14. M / s Ashraf Lone (Irfan) Stat & Gen Store 15 . M/s Bashir Ahmad Mir, Gen. Store 16. M/s Javed Amin Hazkah Enterprises, Kashmir Art Shop 17. M/s Alia Ja, Cosmetic Shop. 
15. Through this communication, the above referred concerns were informed about issuance of tender for allotment of all shops for a period of 11 months vide tender notice No.
Prov/tender-shop/STC- SGR/2016/21686 dated 28/12/2016 until the time the auction process is completed the above named concerns were called upon for payment of rent and other charges for Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
5 the respective shop as per the terms and conditions of the agreement. In addition, the aforesaid concerns were apprised about non-deposit of monthly shop rent for the last few months and calling upon them to deposit due amount of monthly rent by fifth of January 2017. All the aforesaid concerns were also invited to participate in the tender auction to be held on 31 January 2016. 
16. For the reasons best known only to the petitioners, they have not bothered to mention in the writ petition as to which concern of the enlisted 17 business concerns belong to which petitioner as if this task is to be done for them by this court in the writ petition. The reason for not disclosing the petitioners' relation with respect to the above-mentioned concerns is perhaps to hide the fact that may be the petitioners are working said concerns on outsourced basis or having double allotments. 
17. The petitioners have pleaded that some of them are having shops allotted to them by way of allotment orders and/or by way of auction but nevertheless they are depositing the respective rentals continuously exhibited by the rental receipts annexed. All the rental receipts annexed are in the names of the concerns above referred and thus it is not forthcoming from the writ petition as to which rent receipt relates to which of the 14 writ petitioners. 
18. The petitioners have pleaded that the auction exercise undertaken at the end of the respondents qua the shops did not materialize leaving the petitioners to be in continued use and occupation of the shops un-auctioned. In this regard, the petitioners refer to a communication No.
Prov/STC-KMR/Auction/Shop/2017/9919 dated 08/08/2017 of the office of IG STC BSF Kashmir addressed to M/s Shabaz Sultan Wani on the subject of public auction of three (3) number of shops available in the Shopping Complex of BSF Campus Humhama put to auction vide tender notice No.
Prov/Tender-Shops/STC-KMR/2017/8000-07 dated 10th July 2017 and the rejection of bid so submitted by the addressee M/s Shabaz Sultan Wani.
19. What is the relevance of this communication in the context of the petitioners' case is best known only to the petitioners. The petitioners have not clarified as to whom out of them the said communication was referred/addressed. However, one fact is confirmed that the petitioners all along knew the fact very well that the respondents are under an obligation to carry out allotment of shops only through the mode of public auction and not by personal discretion and distribution. 
20. The petitioners in a bid to demonstrate their respective use and occupation of the shops in the said STC BSF Campus have made reference to Communication No. Prov/Civil-shop/STC- KMR/2017/5683-99 dated 10/04/2017 addressed to 17 concerns as named therein and which are as under:
1. M/s Kingfisher Tours and Travels 2. M/s Angle Nidouz Food Court.
3. M/s Rajkumar Tailor Shop,
4. M/s Tamana (Meat Shop)

6 5. M/s Arif Traders (Veg Shop)
6. M/s Adil Nazir (Look at me) Cloth Shop 7. M/s Farooq Dry Fruit Shop 8. M/s Adil Stat & Gift Shop 9. M/s Rajkumar Tailor Shop 10. M/s Javed Akhtar Tailor Shop 11. M/s Krishan Lal Cobbler Shop 12. M/s Shyam Lal Cobbler Shop 13. M/s Md Ashraf Lone (Irfan), Stat & Gen Store 14. M / s Ashraf Lone (Irfan) Stat & Gen Store 15. M/s Shafi, Gen. Store 16. M/s Javed Amin Hazkah Enterprises, Kashmir Art Shop 17. M/s Alia Jan, Cosmetic Shop. 
21. The petitioners have not mentioned in the writ petition which of the above-named concerns relate to which of the petitioners. Through this communication, the concerns aforementioned were called up to make deposit of the Fixed Deposit 3 months' rent as security money. 
22. The petitioners are pleading in the writ petition that while on one hand they were getting assurance from the respondents' end that they will not be making any further auction and that the said auction was going to be one-time for the petitioners to avail to their long-term benefit but on the other hand the respondents was engaged in issuing fresh tenders and that being the impugned tender notice No. Prov/Tender-Shop/STC-KMR/2017/19226-35 dated 30/12/2017 issued for conducting auction of civil shops in the STC BSF Campus Humhama.
23. Upon issuance of the aforesaid tender notice, the petitioners being in a state of concern, are said to have approached the respondents No. 3 & 4 and with oral requests and reminding them of the promise extended by them in favour of the petitioners that there would be no further auction and that the petitioners would continue to be in possession of the shops on enhanced rentals as per the norms fixed by the CPWD.
Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
7 The petitioners thereupon even came to make a written representation signed by 17 signatories to the Inspector General BSF, STC Srinagar stating therein that the petitioners came to provide facilities to the BSF personnels during peak risk times giving the petitioners to understand that they would continue to be in use and occupation of the shops just on periodic rent hike of 10% and that in case the intended auction exercise is carried out that would be against the interest of the petitioners and the promise extended to them. The petitioners through this representation thus sought the withdrawal of the auction notice dated 30/12/2017. 
24. In terms of the impugned tender notice No. Prov/Tender- Shop/STC-KMR/2017/19226-35 dated 30/12/2017, the date of auction was scheduled to be 25th of January 2018. 
25. Thus, in order to preempt and checkmate the said tender notice and the auction exercise intended thereunder by the respondent No.3- IG BSF STC Humhama Srinagar, the petitioners came forward with present writ petition and were able to earn an ex parte direction in terms of an order dated 11/01/2018 ( wrongly typed as January 11th, 2017) in terms whereof status quo existing as on said date was directed to be maintained vis--vis the shops allotted and possessed by the petitioners . On the strength of this order, the petitioners have been able to stretch their continued use and occupation of the shops in the STC BSF Campus Humhama during the course of pendency of this writ petition which has lasted full seven (7) years in running. 
26. As against very vague and unrefined averments based and drawn from writ petition of the writ petitioners, the writ respondents came forward with their joint reply/objections filed on 24/04/2018 setting out writ situation in its essential elements stating that the BSF's Subsidiary Training Centre (STC) was established in June 1990 at Humhama, district Budgam, (Srinagar) in khasra number 424 and that it was in the year 2010 in view of the state of militancy obtaining in Kashmir Valley posing risk to stationed Security Forces including BSF Campus housed BSF personnel and their families, it was decided and done that eight (8) permanent structure shops and six (6) temporary structure shops were put up within the campus in the year 2010 for which purpose the civilians were invited to run the amenity shops to cater to the needs of the STC BSF Campus stationed personnels and their families. The formal inauguration of the STC BSF Campus shopping complex is said to have taken place on 31st March 2010. 
27. The respondents have admitted that to begin with no rental was being charged from the shopkeepers running the shops but only when for the first time in the year 2012 a report No.
PAD/7/09- 11/AALEP/BSF/STC-SGR/2012/195 dated 10/02/2012 of the Internal Audit Party (IAP)
of HQ DG BSF New Delhi with respect to STC BSF Humhama for the period October 2009 to September 2011 in terms of its reference in para 3.3 had registered an objection that five (5) shops have been opened without any prior sanction and no rent and allied charges were being recovered from the occupants of the shops in the said campus, that resulted into an exercise by the establishment of BSF in Srinagar to assess the actual requirements of the shops at Humhama Campus and also to fix rent and electricity charges for the use and occupation of the said shops and to prepare draft agreement to be entered and executed by its current/ prospective allottee/s.
Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
8 28. Based upon this exercise, it was in the year 2013 that from the end of the respondent No. 3 notices for recovery of old dues of rent and electricity charges were issued against each petitioner asking payment of rental as well as electricity charges right from 2010 to October 2013 and also to make deposit of advance rent and electricity charges for the next three months on reckoning basis from October of every year. 
29. Individual notices dated 07/10/2013 to all the shopkeepers, including the petitioners, were sent and served for clearing the old rent dues and electricity charges with effect from 01/04/2010 to 30/06/2013 in three (3) equal instalments in October, November and December 2013. It was only upon deposit of said arrears that the use and occupation of the shops for next 11 months was to be availed by the sitting shopkeepers. The duration of use and occupation of the shops was conveyed to be for 11 months with 10% hike for the next allotment of 11 months. 
30. It was also observed and documented at the end of the respondents that there was no procedure pertaining to allocation of shops in the STC BSF Campus Srinagar. It was also observed that from the record there was forthcoming no fixed date with respect to the allocation of the shops qua the petitioners. 
31. The shopkeepers who were put on said notice did not respond with timely and full deposit of arrears and dues, rent and electricity. Fourteen (14) shop occupants were identified from whom recovery of rental and electricity charges aggregating to an amount of 15,38,740 was to be carried out. 
32. In March and July 2014, individual notices were again issued to the shopkeepers seeking deposit of areas from 2013 and 2014. Frontier Headquarter BSF Kashmir constituted a Board of Officers to fix the monthly rent and electricity charges of civil shops and to prepare memorandum of understanding to be executed with the shopkeepers upon allotment of the shops. 
33. In April 2015, a Board of Officers in its meeting is said to have assessed the rate of rent and approved draft of fresh agreement/contract for the shops inside STC BSF Campus. Thirteen (13)
shopkeepers in the STC BSF Campus were identified who were in use and occupation without any agreement. 
34. In November 2016, a Board of Officers was constituted to undertake rent assessment and preparation of fresh agreement/ contract in draft form for the use and occupation of the civil shops inside BSF campus. Seventeen (17) shopkeepers by business name reference were found to be in use and occupation of the shops without any agreement. 
35. Vide a Tender Notice No. Prov/Tender-Shop/STC- SGR/2016/21686-93 dated 28/12/2016 issued by the DIG STC BSF Srinagar, the auction of 17 shops in terms of its use and occupation was intended for which auction exercise was to be conducted on 31/01/2017. 
36. As a result of auction so conducted on 31/01/2017 with respect to seventeen (17) shops, auction for shop No. 11 was unsuccessful and for shops No. 1 & 16 the two successful bidders failed to Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
9 deposit requisite documents whereas for rest of fourteen (14) shops agreements came to be made with the allottees and that is how the petitioners came to be allottees out of said auction process. 
This auction of shops was for use and occupation for a period of 11 months. All the petitioners came to execute written agreements in March 2017 for use and occupation of respective allotted shop for a duration of 11 months. In this regard the respondents have referred to the following agreements petitioner-wise:
A) Petitioner No. 2 Mudassir Ahmad Rather for Shop No. 1. B) Petitioner No. 3 Raj Kumar for Shop No. 3 & 9. C) Petitioner No. 5 Arif Ahmad Khan for Shop No. 5. D)
Petitioner No. 6 Adil Nazir Wani for Shop No. 6 & 8. E) Petitioner No. 7 Farooq Ahmad Kuchey for Shop No. 7. F) Petitioner No. 8 Javaid Akhtar for Shop No. 10. G)
Petitioner No. 9 Sham Lal for Shop No. 4 & 12. H) Petitioner No. 10 Mohd. Ashraf Lone for Shop No.13. I) Petitioner No. 11 Mehrab Lone for Shop No. 14. J) Petitioner No. 12 Mohd. Shafi Wani for Shop No. 15. H) Petitioner No. 14 Aaliya Jan for Shop No. 17.
37. In July 2017, a fresh auction for the vacant three (3) shops was also done in which the petitioner No. 1 was the highest bidder for Rs. 9000/- for Shop No. 1 but below the reserve price of rupees 20,000/- so the bid was cancelled and the bids for Shops No. 11 & 16 were shelved due to poor competitive response. As the bids for the said three shops failed, so their previous occupants that is the petitioner 1 for Shop No. 1 and the petitioner No. 13 for shop No. 16 were allowed to continue and use an occupation till next auction with 10% hike in monthly rent and making fresh agreement for the period but the petitioners 1 and 13 did not come to sign the requisite documents. 
38. It was in the backdrop of the aforesaid situation when the previous allotment duration of 11 months' use and occupation was to expire in February 2018 that the Tender Notice No.
Prov/Tender- Shop/STC-KMR/2017/19226-35 dated 30/12/2017 came to be issued from the respondent No. 3's end only to get entangled in the litigation generated through the medium of present writ petition. 
39. Upon hearing the submissions from both sides and going through the writ pleadings and the documents therewith and also the record produced by Mr. T.M.Shamsi learned DSGI, this court cannot resist to hold that the petitioners are not only trying to approbate and reprobate but also to exploit the leniency/accommodation on the part of the authorities of the time in charge of the administration of the STC BSF Campus Humhama which condoned the acts of omission and commission at the end of the petitioners in not coming forward even with timely and full payment of rent dues and allied charges making the authorities concerned to literally beg for the clearance of said arrears and dues whereas on the other hand the petitioners kept on enjoying the use of shop spaces for their respective business and benefit.
40. When this court examines the writ petition filed by the petitioners, what is forthcoming as a first hand impression is fact deficiency in the writ petition which, as it is, by no stretch of claim on the part of the petitioners could entitle them to expect earning of the reliefs as prayed for in writ petition. 
Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
10 41 There are fourteen (14) writ petitioners meaning thereby holders of 14 shops in the STC BSF Campus Humhama. Not even a single line whisper averment has been made by and for each petitioner as to when and how he/she first came to be in use and occupation of shop in the STC BSF Campus Humhama and for which business purpose and what was the status of use and occupation at the time of filing of writ petition. So, the petitioners, in fact, have failed their own cause by a state of writ pleading which is framed more to create an illusion as if the petitioners were vested with some perpetual assurance and grant by the respondents with respect to running of the shops in the said STC BSF Campus. None of the fourteen (14) petitioners has pleaded as to whether he/she has any rent arrears outstanding against him/her or not. 
42 The petitioners have not pleaded, rather avoided pleading, that when similar auction exercise was done vide Tender Notice No. Prov/Tender-Shop/STC-SGR/2016/21686 dated 28/12/2016 in which they came to earn allotment of the shops for period of 11 months reckoning from March 2017 onwards then why they did not lodge their protest to the respondents that they cannot resort to auction of the shops in view of the use and occupation of the shops being with the petitioners allegedly reckoning from 1990 onwards when good number of writ petitioners were in their age of minority. 
43 Thus, the petitioners intend to exploit the very fact that somehow their chance coming into use and occupation of the shops even if before 2010 at the STC BSF Campus for doing the business thereat shall now result into a permanence of their respective business establishment just by demand of 10% hike in rental charges and letting them to stay in the shops on perpetual basis. This expectation of the petitioners is misconceived firstly there is no factual basis set up for this expectation to show its basis and secondly article 14 of the Constitution of India binds the respondents to deal and handle the State's largesse and assets in a fair and open manner even in the matter of its allotments by public competitive auction. To accede to the petitioners' plea would be to issue a writ running contrary to the mandate of article 14 of the Constitution of India. 
44. From the pleadings in the writ petition, this court is not able to trace and find out factual much less a legal basis for the petitioners to entertain at their respective a legitimate expectation that the allotment of the shops shall continue to stay with the petitioners leaving no discretion at the end of the respondent No. 3 to go for its year ending auction process. The petitioners, in fact, are meaning to monopolize their gathering at the STC BSF Campus Humhama and that is the reason the petitioners have even come in the present writ petition in a herd manner rather than coming individually bearing respective position statement to salvage situation for oneself by special equity of the individual case.
45. This court finds that the petitioners have also not come clean in their case in the present writ petition. Nowhere the petitioners have referred to the fact that they all had entered into respective written agreements with the STC BSF Kashmir Humhama in March 2017 for the use and occupation of respective shops thereunder for 11 months period subject to payment of rental and other charges. 
By attributing their participation to auction process held in January 2017 to be under a purported impression and understanding the petitioners are meaning to exploit their self-entertained wrong and misconceived impression and expectation that their one time participation in the auction Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/
11 exercise with respect to the shops in reference would earn in their favour a lifelong allotment. 46 The petitioners have not pleaded and cannot be heard to plead that it was and is in the legal competence and authority of the BSF Establishment to extend any such assurance or promise in favour of the petitioners with respect to their all time use and occupation of the shops in reference. 
Even if any official/authority of the and at the end of the BSF would have ever extended any such assurance or promise from his end to the petitioners still that would not have meant to be binding to the successors-in-office who are to act and conduct the office and authority in accordance with law with respect to the allotment of the shops. 
47. The petitioners are also making a very feeble attempt to suggest but not saying expressly that the respondents are bound by a promissory estoppel in the favour of the petitioners and cannot disown the petitioners of their respective claims to enjoy the use and occupation of the respective shops as the petitioners had purportedly acted upon an assurance from the respondents' end that the petitioners need to bear with one time auction exercise by the respondents so as to set their record straight and that was the reason for the petitioners to participate in the auction process in 2017 which otherwise they would not have joined. 48 The petitioners are chasing a mirage simply to say. 
By no stretch of claim or authority, the petitioners can be allowed to say that they had an estoppel like situation in their favour. Who was the particular BSF official/s, and of which tenure posting,
who had made the petitioners to act and stay under such a false impression has not been spelled out by the petitioners so the respondents can not be called upon to meet such a purported plea of the petitioners. 
49. Otherwise also, it is not for the petitioners to usurp the decision making of the respondents as to the manner in which the respondents intend to administer and manage the STC BSF Campus,
Humhama in the context of the shops thereat .
